_comment: Events happening in or near the forest. Manually researched and verified on lastVerified; not yet fed by an automated script (see spec/spec-weekly-report.md).

entries.title: Epping Forest Wildwood Trail Series: Half Marathon & 10K
entries.body: A trail half marathon (9:00 start) and 10K (9:30 start) through Epping Forest, chip-timed, with aid stations and limited parking. Entry around £37, ages 17+.

entries.title: Top Picks: litter pick at Hollow Ponds
entries.body: Free, volunteer-run litter pick at Hollow Ponds, part of the Epping Forest charity's recurring 'Top Picks' series.

entries.title: Apple Day at Copped Hall
entries.body: Family event in the Mansion and gardens at Copped Hall: apple identification by an orchard expert, produce and plant stalls, live music (Chingford Morris Men, Harlow Brass Band) and children's entertainment. Gates open 11am, last entry 4pm. Tickets £12 in advance or £15 on the day; free for Friends of Copped Hall, under-18s and carers.

entries.title: Archives on Show: Epping Forest
entries.place: The London Archives, 40 Northampton Road, EC1R 0HB
entries.body: Free, one-hour drop-in sessions (1pm or 2pm) on Epping Forest's archives, run on multiple dates. Check the listing for the next date -- none is reliably current as of this verification.
entries.reverificationNote: No specific upcoming date confirmed -- re-check the listing for the next session before using in a report.

entries.title: Theydon Bois Christmas lights and market
entries.place: Village Hall, Coppice Row, Theydon Bois
entries.body: Friday 27 November: Christmas lights and the primary school choir at the Village Hall at 5pm, followed by the village Christmas market from 5.30pm to 8pm.
entries.locationSource: nominatim: Village Hall, Coppice Row, Theydon Bois

entries.title: Waltham Abbey Cavalcade of Light
entries.body: The Cavalcade of Light takes place on Friday 27 November. Check the council listing for the route and timings.

entries.title: Epping Christmas Market
entries.body: Friday 4 December, noon to 8pm: a traditional Christmas market with entertainment, food, gifts, crafts, Santa and festive fun.

entries.title: Highams Park Christmas Fayre
entries.body: Sunday 6 December, 11am to 5pm: a free Christmas fayre for all the family. Check the community calendar for locations and activities.

entries.title: Loughton Christmas Fair and Market
entries.place: Staples Road Primary School, Loughton, IG10 1HR
entries.body: Sunday 6 December, noon to 3pm: free entry to the Staples Road School PTA Christmas fair, with stalls, games, performances and refreshments from the 41st Epping Forest Scouts.
entries.locationSource: nominatim: Staples Road Primary School, Loughton, IG10 1HR

entries.title: Waltham Abbey Christmas Market
entries.place: Sun Street and Market Square, Waltham Abbey
entries.body: Saturday 12 December, 9am to 3pm: Christmas market on Sun Street and Market Square.

entries.title: North Chingford Christmas Market
entries.place: Chingford Assembly Hall and The Green
entries.body: Saturday 19 December, 11am to 4pm: free-entry market with more than 30 stalls, live entertainment and community carols. Santa’s grotto supports The Dream Factory and requires a separate advance booking.

sourceNotes.source: City of London: Epping Forest & Commons Committee (EFCC) 'Committee Events Diary'
sourceNotes.note: The single best structured events source found: a detailed month-by-month diary (exhibitions, guided tours, litter picks, youth conservation sessions, volunteering) published as a PDF alongside each committee meeting's agenda pack on democracy.cityoflondon.gov.uk. No stable URL -- a new PDF is published at each meeting (next: 2026-11-02), so a script would need to find the committee's current agenda page (search 'Epping Forest Commons Committee' on democracy.cityoflondon.gov.uk) and pull the latest 'Diary' attachment. Worth building a scraper for.

sourceNotes.source: Eventbrite organiser 'Epping Forest' (collections: Festive Forest, Top Picks, Leaky Dam Building)
sourceNotes.note: Real and current, but an API key would not improve on scraping the public pages: Eventbrite retired public cross-organiser event search from its v3 API in February 2020. The remaining API only lists events for an organisation/account you yourself control (GET /v3/organizations/{id}/events/) -- there's no approval tier that reopens access to another organiser's calendar, and 'Epping Forest' is not our account. An OAuth app (the application URL + redirect URI Eventbrite's developer portal asks for) buys nothing here. Scraping the public collection pages, as done for this file, remains the only option.

sourceNotes.source: https://www.eventbrite.co.uk/o/9768889881 (Eventbrite organiser page, 'Epping Forest')
sourceNotes.note: The weekly run checks this organiser page every run as a public page, plus each upcoming event's detail page; there is no API option (see the Eventbrite organiser note above). It was not fetchable from the authoring session's network, so reachability from the workflow is unverified. If blocked, treat it as an access limitation, not as proof of no events.

sourceNotes.source: cityoflondon.gov.uk/.../whats-new-in-epping-forest
sourceNotes.note: Good general-interest page (reminders, long-running works, car park/riding/fishing notices -- see data/forest-notices.json) but it's a single long page with no dates on most items and no RSS feed, so it suits a human skim better than automated diffing.

sourceNotes.source: eppingforestdc.gov.uk/whats-on-in-epping-forest
sourceNotes.note: District council activities (not City of London / forest-specific) with no dates or locations on the page itself -- detail is locked in a brochure PDF. Lower value for forest-specific events than the EFCC diary.

sourceNotes.source: coppedhalltrust.org.uk (own site, e.g. the Apple Day article)
sourceNotes.note: Copped Hall is independently run by its own trust, not City of London, so it never appears in the EFCC diary above -- this is the first entry sourced from a venue-specific site rather than a forest-wide aggregator. It's a plain CMS article per event, no calendar index or RSS found, so a script would have no list of 'current article ids' to crawl; finding new events still means someone (or the weekly research step) visiting the site. Worth re-checking each run rather than building a scraper for yet. The same is likely true of other independently-run sites inside or near the boundary (visitor centres, heritage trusts) that this run hasn't individually surveyed.

sourceNotes.source: Facebook pages of forest-adjacent organisations (e.g. Epping Forest Heritage Trust)
sourceNotes.note: Not usable, by API or by scraping. Meta has gated the Graph API's 'Page Public Content Access' behind App Review and Business Verification since 2018 (post-Cambridge Analytica), so there is no keyless or simple-OAuth way to read an arbitrary public Page's posts. Fetching a post's own URL without being logged in confirms this in practice: the page returns only its title, no post body, date or details. A human can still open the page and read it; nothing here is automatable.

sourceNotes.source: X/Twitter accounts of forest-adjacent organisations
sourceNotes.note: Not usable for free. X removed free read access in 2023; reading another account's posts (search or timeline) now needs at minimum the paid Basic tier, priced per month rather than per use, which is a standing cost for monitoring accounts that mostly repeat what their own websites or Facebook pages already say. Not worth it unless a specific account turns out to be the only place an event is announced.

sourceNotes.source: Wanstead Village Directory events calendar (wansteadvillagedirectory.com/events/ -- covers Wanstead and Wanstead Park, the forest's southern tip)
sourceNotes.note: A real, directly-fetchable, VERIFIED source: its WordPress 'The Events Calendar' plugin exposes a plain iCal feed at https://wansteadvillagedirectory.com/events/list/?ical=1 -- fetched and parsed on 2026-10-10 and confirmed to contain an actual VEVENT for 'Wanstead Beer Festival 2026' (DTSTART 2026-10-10T13:00 Europe/London, at Christ Church Hall, Wanstead), the event that went unnoticed and prompted this evaluation (github.com/simonmcmanus/epping-forest-finds/issues/192). This supersedes an earlier, unverified note in this file pointing at a different Wanstead calendar (Wansteadium's, run through a public Google Calendar) which was never actually confirmed to carry the festival -- don't resurrect that one without verifying its content first.

sourceNotes.source: Visit Epping Forest events calendar (visiteppingforest.org/events/whats-on/events-calendar)
sourceNotes.note: The official Epping Forest District tourism site. A plain page with no feed, but its event list (dates, venue, description) is present in the raw HTML rather than requiring JavaScript, so it scrapes the same way Copped Hall's site does. Broader than any single town's listing: covers venues across the whole district, including Copped Hall and Epping Ongar Railway. Rechecked 2026-11-15: dated Christmas listings include Waltham Abbey, Abridge and Chigwell Hall markets, Ongar lights festival and railway Santa specials. Check all results pages and event detail pages, not only the calendar landing page.

sourceNotes.source: Epping Town Council events diary (eppingtowncouncil.gov.uk/Events_Diary_35167.aspx)
sourceNotes.note: Already a required weekly source. Its indexed diary confirms Epping Christmas Market on 4 December 2026, noon-8pm. Direct WebFetch returned HTTP 403 on 2026-11-15; use current indexed council text for discovery and seek organiser corroboration if details cannot be fetched. Do not roll forward dates or switch-on times from older leaflets.

sourceNotes.source: Epping Ongar Railway (eorailway.co.uk) -- heritage railway in the district running galas and a Real Ale and Cider Weekend
sourceNotes.note: A real, forest-district-relevant venue, but eorailway.co.uk returned HTTP 503 to a direct automated fetch (both the events page and the site root) -- likely bot-blocking rather than the site being down, since the same content is reachable via search-engine caches and third-party listings (raildays.org). Covered indirectly via the Visit Epping Forest calendar above for now; worth re-testing eorailway.co.uk directly on a future run in case the block lifts.

sourceNotes.source: Loughton Town Council, Waltham Forest borough-wide listings, Chigwell Parish Council and Chingford Historical Society
sourceNotes.note: Retain as secondary research pages; no working syndicated feed confirmed. Do not confuse the lack of a feed with a lack of events: check current dated HTML pages and organiser sites. The October assessment of Theydon Bois is superseded by its accessible calendar below; Waltham Abbey is assessed separately below.

sourceNotes.source: South Woodford Village Gazette events calendar (swvg.co.uk/events/ -- covers South Woodford, Woodford Green, Snaresbrook and Aldersbrook)
sourceNotes.note: A second real, directly-fetchable, VERIFIED source, same WordPress 'The Events Calendar' plugin as the Wanstead Village Directory above: a plain iCal feed at https://swvg.co.uk/events/list/?ical=1, fetched and parsed on 2026-10-10 and confirmed to contain real, dated VEVENTs. It covers Woodford Green (one of the coverage settlements) as well as Wanstead -- and some Wanstead events, including the Beer Festival itself, appear in both this feed and the Wanstead Village Directory feed above, so a run checking both must de-dupe by title+date rather than add each twice.

sourceNotes.source: Waltham Abbey Town Council's own events page (walthamabbey-tc.gov.uk/events/)
sourceNotes.note: The current council events index is search-indexed with dated 2026 listings: Cavalcade of Light on 27 November and Christmas Market on 12 December, 9am-3pm, on Sun Street and Market Square. Direct fetching of /events still returned HTTP 403 on 2026-11-15; a working iCal feed is not verified. Use current indexed council listings for discovery and cross-check Visit Epping Forest or the organiser before publication. Avoid the undated /the-council/cavalcade-and-festival-of-light page, which still gives different dates without a year.

sourceNotes.source: Essex Libraries 'Events & Bookings' site (library-events.essex.gov.uk) -- lists events at Loughton, Buckhurst Hill, Chigwell, Waltham Abbey and Epping library branches among others
sourceNotes.note: Real and current (e.g. storytimes, a Peabody advice drop-in, dementia information sessions), and genuinely covers five of the coverage settlements from one site -- but it's a room-booking engine with per-branch/per-event pages, not a syndicated calendar, and no RSS/iCal feed was found on the page. Worth a human skim per branch; not scriptable as a single feed yet.

sourceNotes.source: Chigwell Parish Council and Chingford Historical Society (chingfordhistory.org.uk)
sourceNotes.note: Chigwell PC's site follows the same ASP.NET council-CMS pattern as Loughton's (news-style display pages, no feed found). Chingford Historical Society runs real, dated events (heritage talks, a Heritage Festival, a downloadable annual talks programme) but publishes them as a plain 'Calendar of Events' page with no RSS/iCal feed -- worth a human skim, same treatment as Copped Hall's site.

sourceNotes.source: Village halls at North Weald, Abridge, Nazeing and High Beach
sourceNotes.note: Searched for each by name; found only charity-register contact details and occasional third-party mentions (e.g. a 2025 barn dance at Abridge via a constituency MP's site), no own event listing or feed for any of the four. Lower priority than the named coverage settlements -- not worth further research time unless a specific event is reported missing from one of them.

sourceNotes.source: Bedford House / Buckhurst Hill Community Association (bedfordhouse.org.uk)
sourceNotes.note: A real, active local charity (adult education classes, an 'Upcoming Events' section, named events like a Winter Fair) -- the best Buckhurst Hill-specific lead found, better than the generic aggregator noise that name alone turns up. Its homepage links to separate Courses & Activities / Upcoming Events / Past Events pages rather than listing them directly, and guessing the events page's URL (bedfordhouse.org.uk/events) 404s, so its actual events page path and whether it carries a feed are still unconfirmed. Worth finding the right URL and checking properly on a future run rather than re-searching from scratch.

sourceNotes.source: Theydon Bois Parish Council calendar (https://theydonbois-pc.gov.uk/events/month/)
sourceNotes.note: Accessible dated HTML calendar verified 2026-11-15, superseding the October assessment of its old news category. Lists the 27 November 2026 Christmas market: lights and choir 5pm, stalls 5.30pm-8pm. The calendar slot starts at 5pm; retain the distinction in event prose. /events/list/?ical=1 could not be accessed by the web tool, so an iCal feed remains unverified; use HTML now.

sourceNotes.source: Highams Park Portal (https://highamspark.london/events/)
sourceNotes.note: Accessible dated community calendar verified 2026-11-15. December calendar lists the free Christmas Fayre on 6 December 2026, 11am-5pm, plus local performances. Useful for the southern forest edge. Read event details for locations; a working syndicated feed has not been verified.

sourceNotes.source: Love Chingford (https://chingfordmarket.com/) and The Dream Factory (https://www.yourdreamfactory.org/the-dream-factory-santas-grotto)
sourceNotes.note: Both accessible organiser/charity HTML pages agree on North Chingford Christmas Market at Assembly Hall and The Green, 19 December 2026, 11am-4pm. Free market entry; grotto needs separate advance booking. Use the charity events index for additional local fundraisers. No feed verified; do not rely on social posts.

sourceNotes.source: 41st Epping Forest Scouts events (https://www.41steppingforestscouts.org.uk/events)
sourceNotes.note: Accessible dated organiser-participant HTML listings verified 2026-11-15. Confirms the Staples Road School PTA fair on 6 December 2026, noon-3pm, free entry. Covers community/school fairs that broader tourism calendars can miss; distinguish public fairs from member-only activities. No feed verified.
